prompt: We're about to put an LLM agent live on Binance USD-M perps (BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT). It runs in an OpenClaw-style setup: the LLM proposes trades through tool calls to a local executor, and we've installed two community skills from a marketplace for news sentiment and on-chain signals. Before it touches real money, write a design doc, risk_execution_design.md, for the execution/risk layer: which checks go where, concrete default numbers, what happens in high-volatility or low-margin conditions, and how we test that it actually holds up against bad or manipulated LLM output. Include a short Python sketch of the core check (save it as gate_sketch.py).
assertions: Puts a deterministic, non-bypassable gate between the LLM/strategy and the exchange executor
Treats LLM output and the marketplace skills as untrusted (prompt injection and supply-chain risk addressed)
Tightens limits based on trust signals (skill provenance, injection alerts or source reliability)
Clamps over-limit requests down to allowed size (partial approval), not only reject
Gives concrete leverage caps that tighten in high-volatility regimes
Gives concrete cooldown and order-rate limits
Uses allowlists for tools/venues/symbols (e.g. only BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT, no withdrawals)
Defines a reduce-only state for low margin and/or extreme volatility or drawdown
Accounts for funding payments and/or maintenance-margin/liquidation mechanics
Logs an audit record per decision (rule hit, budgets/limits, state snapshot)
Test plan includes parameter escalation, order flooding/rapid flipping, and tool/venue misuse attacks
Test metrics include both attack success (leakage) and false blocks of legitimate orders
